procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: Writ Petition (Civil) No. 12739 was filed directly in the Supreme Court.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: An entity is entitled to take any action it deems appropriate, including the revocation of a consent order.
obiter: The purpose of such action is to eliminate hazard to the public.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: All Expert Committees are unanimous in their view that by adopting proper and adequate safety measures, the element of risk to the workmen and the public can only be minimised, but it cannot be totally eliminated. The general concensus of opinion of all the Expert Committees is that relocation of the caustic chlorine plant is the only long term solution, if hazard to the community is to be completely eliminated. Whether the caustic chlorine plant should be directed to be shifted or relocated at a place where there will be no hazard to the community and if so, within what time-frame, is a question which will require serious consideration and a National Policy will have to be evolved by the Government for location of toxic or hazardous industries.
why_appellant_lost: The argument for permanent closure was countered by the severe socio-economic consequences, including the unemployment of about 4,000 workmen and the disruption of chlorine supply to the Delhi Water Supply Undertaking.
why_respondent_won: The management had complied with all the recommendations made in the reports of the Manmohan Singh Committee and Nilay Choudhary Committee, and had taken every possible step and measure for the purpose of ensuring complete safety in the operation of the caustic chlorine plant.

The court considered the significant negative impacts of a permanent closure, such as the loss to the company, unemployment for approximately 4,000 workers, and the disruption of essential supplies like chlorine for the Delhi Water Supply Undertaking and other downstream products.
policy_considerations: A National Policy will have to be evolved by the Government for location of toxic or hazardous industries and a decision will have to be taken in regard to relocation of such industries with a view to eliminating risk to the community likely to arise from the operation of such industries.

The court must weigh the risk to the community against the consequences of closing the plant, which would result not only in loss to the company but also in unemployment of about 4,000 workmen and non-availability of chlorine to Delhi Water Supply Under-taking and short supply of down stream products.

The court recognized the signal service to the community rendered by the petitioner in bringing the public interest litigation, which led to improvements in the design, structure, and quality of the machinery and equipment in the caustic chlorine plant and pressured the management to observe safety standards.
